An agent’s answers depend on the evidence it can retrieve. When that evidence is incomplete or irrelevant, the agent will repeat searches and inspect additional documents, consuming more inference tokens before completing the task. Better retrieval can help agents reach grounded answers with fewer wasted tokens. At enterprise scale, that waste leads to massive inefficiencies. Agents need the right retrieval models and systems to reach insights faster.

Today, we are expanding the Nemotron Retriever collection with new open, commercially available models for embedding, reranking, and document extraction. The new models include Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B BF16, 1B BF16, 1B NVFP4, Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B BF16, and Nemotron 3.5 Parse at 631M parameters.

Together, these state-of-the-art models bring multimodal retrieval, relevance ranking, and document processing to enterprise agent workflows.

Better Retrieval for More Efficient Agents

Retrieval quality affects both the answers an agent produces and the LLM inference cost. Relevant evidence can help the agent answer a question or better decide its next step, and reranking improves the quality of evidence that enters its context.

Consider an agent asked to identify products at risk of stockouts next quarter and explain why. It must combine demand forecasts in charts, inventory levels in tables, and supplier lead times in reports, then reason about whether replenishment will arrive before inventory runs out. Completing the task requires finding the relevant evidence across documents and using it together in the analysis.

To understand how retrieval affects the agent’s ability to combine evidence and complete a task, we evaluated Nemotron 3.5 Embed and Rerank across ViDoRe v3, BRIGHT, and BrowseComp-Plus. ViDoRe v3 uses combined text and image inputs, while BRIGHT and BrowseComp-Plus use text-only inputs. In this pipeline, an agent queries the corpus using a search tool, inspects the evidence, and refines its next search attempt to find the most relevant information to a given query. The experiments below vary how the search tool is implemented: embedding only, embedding plus reranking, and with different models for each. The LLM powering the agent, tools, task set, corpus, and execution policy remain fixed while the retrieval configuration changes. We measure the agent's ability to find the relevant information for each task and total agent inference tokens per task, including input and output tokens across all turns.

Figure 1. End-to-end task success versus total agent inference tokens per task across retrieval configurations.

  • Lower agent inference cost: Adding Nemotron 3.5 Rerank reduces agentic token cost per query by approximately 14% with Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B, and 13% with Nemotron 3.5 Embed 1B, while improving retrieval accuracy in both configurations.
  • Better evidence within the same agent budget: With Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B as the retriever, Nemotron 3.5 Rerank delivered approximately 0.9 points higher nDCG@10 than Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B at a similar agentic token cost.

Nemotron 3.5 Embed and Rerank

Behind these agent successes are Nemotron 3.5 Embed and Nemotron 3.5 Rerank, which retrieve evidence across text and images and prioritize it for the agent’s context. Nemotron 3.5 Embed builds on the previous generation’s Nemotron 3 Embed text embedding models to retrieve evidence from document images, including tables, charts, infographics, datasheets, and schematics. This allows applications to search information conveyed by visual content alongside document text.

The four models provide different options for retrieval and second-stage ranking:

Key features include:

  • Text and image retrieval: Search document text and images containing tables, charts, infographics, datasheets, and schematics.
  • Multilingual support: Text retrieval was evaluated across 34 languages, while multilingual visual retrieval was evaluated on MIRACL Vision (18 languages) and KoViDoRe. The model may support additional languages beyond those evaluated.
  • Multimodal reranking: An 8B cross-encoder scores query–document pairs across text and image inputs.
  • BF16 and NVFP4 deployment: The 1B embedding model is available in BF16 and NVFP4, with quantization applied to both text and image encoders.
  • Domain adaptation: Nemotron embedding fine-tuning recipes support custom document collections, with a 18% and 3% relative nDCG@10 gain for Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16 and Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16 respectively in our chart and infographic experiments.

Leading Multimodal Dense Retrieval on ViDoRe v3

On ViDoRe v3.1, Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B BF16 achieves 61.17 nDCG@10, ranking first among dense retrieval models. This is an 8.94-point improvement over the 52.23 score achieved by the Llama Nemotron Embed VL 1B model. The 1B model brings most of this visual retrieval quality into a smaller model. Distilled from the 8B teacher, Nemotron 3.5 Embed 1B BF16 scores 58.38 nDCG@10, retaining 95.4% of the teacher’s score.

Figure 2. Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B BF16 ranked first among dense retrieval models on the ViDoRe v3.1 leaderboard as of 10/20/2026.

We also compare the models with Qwen3-VL-Embedding, EmbeddingGemma-2, and the previous-generation NVIDIA model across ViDoRe v3, Korean ViDoRe and MIRACL Vision. The chart below reports retrieval accuracy for image-only and combined image-and-text inputs.

Figure 3. Text and visual retrieval performance of Nemotron 3.5 Embed compared with prior-generation models and selected baselines.

The multilingual results show how the models retrieve evidence across different language settings. On MIRACL Vision, the 8B model achieves 72.6 nDCG@10, exceeding Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B by 4.3 points. We also evaluate the models on KoViDoRe; both Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B and 1B outperform the Qwen baselines when using combined image and text inputs.

Reranking the Evidence for Agent Tasks

Embedding models make large collections searchable by representing content as vectors. After retrieval returns a candidate set, Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B BF16 evaluates each candidate against the query to refine the ordering across text and image inputs. By distinguishing broadly related content from evidence that directly answers the question, the reranker helps agents use their context budget more effectively and focus on information needed to complete the task. For agentic retrieval systems, surfacing the strongest evidence earlier can reduce distracting context and help agents produce more grounded, efficient responses.

In collaboration with the MTEB team, we are launching the ViDoRe v3.1 reranking leaderboard to benchmark rerankers on document retrieval across image-only, text-only, and combined image-and-text inputs. Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B BF16 achieves 60.49 nDCG@10 with combined image-and-text inputs compared with Qwen-3-VL-Reranker-8B’s 59.17.

Figure 4. Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B-BF16 ranked first on ViDoRe v3.1 Reranking leaderboard as of 10/20/2026.

Figure 5. Text and visual reranker performance of Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B compared with Qwen 3 VL Reranker 8B. Both models reranked the top 50 candidates retrieved by the Nemotron 3.5 Embed 1B model.

Scaling Multimodal Retrieval with NVFP4

Retrieval quality is only part of the equation for production agentic systems. As document collections and query volumes grow, teams must balance accuracy, throughput, and infrastructure requirements.

Nemotron 3.5 Embed 1B NVFP4 provides an optimized deployment option for high-throughput multimodal retrieval. On NVIDIA GB200, it delivers 27.1% higher throughput compared with the 1B BF16 model, increasing from 101.3 to 128.8 documents per second while retaining 99.85% of its retrieval accuracy on ViDoRe v3 with combined image and text inputs. As Figure 6 shows, the NVFP4 model offers a strong accuracy-throughput tradeoff for teams scaling retrieval across production workloads.

This deployment flexibility complements domain-specific customization: teams can select the data type of model weights that fits their infrastructure, then adapt the embedding and reranking models to their own terminology, documents, and retrieval tasks.

Figure 6. ViDoRe V3 retrieval accuracy versus serving efficiency, comparing Nemotron 3.5 Embed with selected smaller open embedding baselines.

High-Performance Serving with NVIDIA NIM

NVIDIA NIM provides a high-performance deployment path for Nemotron 3.5 Embed. In testing on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, NIM delivered 6,031 query requests per second—approximately 2.9× the throughput of a comparable vLLM configuration at 2,099 requests per second—while maintaining comparable passage-processing throughput. This optimized serving stack helps enterprises scale retrieval workloads with production-ready deployment and support.

Figure 7. Nemotron 3.5 Embed NIM serving performance compared with the vLLM checkpoint on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs.

Adapting Retrieval to Domain-Specific Tasks

Enterprise agents often search documents containing specialized terminology and company-specific information that general-purpose retrieval models may not fully capture. Fine-tuning allows teams to adapt Nemotron 3.5 Embed and Rerank using their own documents, queries, and relevance labels to their specific domains and use cases.

The Nemotron multimodal embedding fine-tuning recipe combines synthetic data generation, hard-negative mining, fine-tuning with NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel, and evaluation in one workflow. Teams can generate queries and relevance labels from their own documents to build training data for their retrieval tasks.

We evaluated the recipe on 8,202 chart and infographic images using 8,591 synthetic queries generated with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, focusing on enumerative and open-ended queries with multiple relevant images. Fine-tuning the Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16 on 6,872 queries for one epoch increased nDCG@10 from 37.34 to 44.12, a 18% relative gain over the base model, on 1,719 held-out synthetic queries. Using the same synthetic queries set, fine-tuning Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16 for one epoch increased nDCG@10 from 41.44 to 42.75, a 3% relative gain.

How We Built the Embed and Rerank Models

Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B builds on Ministral-3-8B-Instruct, with its language component initialized from Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16. The model is trained on image and text corpora using contrastive learning to produce representations for multimodal retrieval.

The Embed 1B models are distilled from Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B, with their language component initialized from Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16. Distillation combines cosine and mean squared error (MSE) losses to align the student’s embeddings with the teacher’s.

The language component remains frozen throughout embedding-model training. Text-only embeddings are therefore expected to remain unchanged from the corresponding Nemotron 3 Embed models, allowing existing text embeddings and vector indexes to be reused.

Nemotron 3.5 Rerank uses the same backbone architecture as Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B in a cross-encoder configuration. While the embedding model encodes queries and documents separately and scores their similarity, the reranker jointly encodes each query–document pair. A final multilayer perceptron (MLP) scoring head produces a scalar relevance logit.

All models are trained on a mixture of publicly available and synthetic multilingual, multimodal data, and their final released weights are produced through checkpoint ensembling. Further details on the training data are available in each model’s Hugging Face model card.

Nemotron 3.5 Parse

Enterprise knowledge often arrives in PDFs whose embedded text captures only part of what is on the page. Extracting that text can lose reading order, separate table values from their headers, or omit information conveyed in charts. Scanned documents and image-based PDFs may contain no usable text layer at all. Before this information can support search, retrieval, or automated document workflows, the pixels need to become structured content.

Nemotron 3.5 Parse converts document images into machine-readable text while preserving the structure that gives the content meaning. It identifies document elements, their locations, and reading order, and extracts tables and charts into structured representations. The resulting Markdown, HTML tables, and structured blocks give developers content that is better suited to indexing, search, and downstream processing. Applications can retrieve a passage with its surrounding context, process a table as rows and columns, and link extracted evidence back to its location on the original page.

At 631 million parameters, Nemotron 3.5 Parse brings this capability to document pipelines at scale, complementing Nemotron 3.5 Embed and Rerank with structured information for retrieval and agent workflows.

Leading Accuracy with Faster Document Processing

Figure 8. Nemotron 3.5 Parse ranked first on ParseBench leaderboard among models with fewer than 1 billion parameters as of 10/20/2026.

Nemotron 3.5 Parse ranks #1 on ParseBench among models with fewer than 1 billion parameters, achieving a score of 75.20 while processing 10.5 pages per second on one NVIDIA H100. It delivers best-in-class speed with well optimized parameter allocation, multi-token prediction, speculative decoding and flexible native-resolution handling. ParseBench tests table and chart extraction, content faithfulness, semantic formatting, and visual grounding.

Developers can scale processing toward speed or accuracy using the same model. Single-pass inference extracts each page once for the highest throughput. Double-pass inference revisits tables and charts identified in the initial page parse. Triple-pass inference adds a detection pass to find additional regions for refinement. This approach concentrates additional processing on document regions that benefit from a closer look.

Teams can choose the operating point that fits their workload, from rapid ingestion of large document collections to more detailed extraction of complex pages.

Figure 9. Nemotron Parse 3.5 achieves pareto optimal performance on ParseBench leaderboard.

How We Built Nemotron 3.5 Parse

Nemotron 3.5 Parse is trained on a diverse mixture of enterprise documents, scientific papers, forms, tables, charts, and multilingual text. A strong synthetic data engine expands the range of layouts, structures, and languages the model sees, complementing automatically labeled documents and human-labeled data. Synthetic multilingual data helps build broad OCR capability, with strong performance in evaluations spanning 163 language and script combinations. This diversity prepares the model for the varied content found in enterprise document collections. Model card and multilingual coverage.

We further improve robustness and reliability through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), using custom reward functions to reinforce correct document structure and penalize failures. This post-training reduces repetitive generation loops and unclosed blocks, improves table consistency, and strengthens adherence to chart schemas, making extracted information more reliable for downstream document workflows.

Thank you to LightOn for raising the open-source bar with their models and technical blog. The shared techniques were pivotal in improving our model.

Early Enterprise Partner Evaluations

  • Elastic customers can access NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever embedding and reranking models through Elasticsearch’s Inference API using NVIDIA inference endpoints. Nemotron 3 will be available via Elastic Inference Service (EIS) soon, while support for Nemotron models on-prem deployment is on the roadmap.
  • Vectorize evaluated NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Embed using Hindsight Agent Memory, and it ranked first on two long-conversation memory benchmarks: achieving 93.8% recall@10 on LoCoMo and 65.9% on BEAM 100K against seven other embedding models. It also delivered the highest MRR and recall@5, highlighting its strength for retrieving relevant memories across long, complex conversation histories.
  • Perplexity saw strong results from NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Embed on Q2D-Web, its benchmark for first-stage retrieval in agentic search. On Perplexity's private 72-task reranking benchmark, NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B achieved the highest average score of the rerankers evaluated, with strong results across all six domains. These results show the value of specialized retrieval models alongside decision models like pplx-decider-v1.2. Perplexity looks forward to evaluating the Nemotron 3.5 retrieval suites, and the two companies are in ongoing discussions about deeper technical collaboration.
  • Turbopuffer evaluated NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B on the enterprise PDF search benchmark and found that it provided ~5% more relevant results at Recall@20 than the next best model. These models are SOTA for common business tasks, like searching through PDFs with complex images, and are now available in Turbopuffer native embedding.

Getting Started

Developers can access the open weights, data, training recipes, and more on Hugging Face, deploy the NVIDIA NIM for production inference, or deploy the models through leading AI Cloud and Inference Partners including Baseten (Embed, Rerank, Parse), DeepInfra (Embed 1B, Embed 8B, Rerank 8B), FriendliAI (Embed 1B, Embed 8B, Rerank 8B), and OpenRouter (Embed 1B, Embed 8B, Rerank 8B).

  • Nemotron-3.5-Parse: Hugging Face, NIM
  • Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16: Hugging Face, NIM
  • Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16: Hugging Face, NIM
  • Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-NVFP4: Hugging Face, NIM
  • Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B-BF16: Hugging Face, NIM

For domain adaptation with NVIDIA AutoModel, we provide fine-tuning support for multimodal embedding and reranking, enabling teams to adapt the models to their own document collections and relevance requirements. Get started with the Nemotron embedding and reranking fine-tuning recipes.

Choose a model based on your workflow: Parse for extracting structured information from documents, Embed for searching text and images, and Rerank for improving the ordering of retrieved results. Combine them to build retrieval pipelines that deliver stronger evidence to AI agents.

This deployment flexibility complements domain-specific customization: teams can select the data type of model weights that fits their infrastructure, then adapt the embedding and reranking models to their own terminology, documents, and retrieval tasks.

*Figure 6. ViDoRe V3 retrieval accuracy versus serving efficiency, comparing Nemotron 3.5 Embed with selected smaller open embedding baselines.*

### 
		
	
	
		High-Performance Serving with NVIDIA NIM

NVIDIA NIM provides a high-performance deployment path for Nemotron 3.5 Embed. In testing on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, NIM delivered 6,031 query requests per second—approximately 2.9× the throughput of a comparable vLLM configuration at 2,099 requests per second—while maintaining comparable passage-processing throughput. This optimized serving stack helps enterprises scale retrieval workloads with production-ready deployment and support.

*Figure 7. Nemotron 3.5 Embed NIM serving performance compared with the vLLM checkpoint on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs.*

### 
		
	
	
		Adapting Retrieval to Domain-Specific Tasks

Enterprise agents often search documents containing specialized terminology and company-specific information that general-purpose retrieval models may not fully capture. Fine-tuning allows teams to adapt Nemotron 3.5 Embed and Rerank using their own documents, queries, and relevance labels to their specific domains and use cases.

The [Nemotron multimodal embedding fine-tuning recipe](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Nemotron/tree/main/src/nemotron/recipes/embed) combines synthetic data generation, hard-negative mining, fine-tuning with [NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel](https://github.com/nvidia-nemo/automodel), and evaluation in one workflow. Teams can generate queries and relevance labels from their own documents to build training data for their retrieval tasks.

We evaluated the recipe on 8,202 chart and infographic images using 8,591 synthetic queries generated with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, focusing on enumerative and open-ended queries with multiple relevant images. Fine-tuning the Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16 on 6,872 queries for one epoch increased nDCG@10 from 37.34 to 44.12, a 18% relative gain over the base model, on 1,719 held-out synthetic queries. Using the same synthetic queries set, fine-tuning Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16 for one epoch increased nDCG@10 from 41.44 to 42.75, a 3% relative gain.

### 
		
	
	
		How We Built the Embed and Rerank Models

Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B builds on [Ministral-3-8B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512-BF16), with its language component initialized from [Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16). The model is trained on image and text corpora using contrastive learning to produce representations for multimodal retrieval.

The Embed 1B models are distilled from Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B, with their language component initialized from [Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16). Distillation combines cosine and mean squared error (MSE) losses to align the student’s embeddings with the teacher’s.

The language component remains frozen throughout embedding-model training. Text-only embeddings are therefore expected to remain unchanged from the corresponding Nemotron 3 Embed models, allowing existing text embeddings and vector indexes to be reused.

Nemotron 3.5 Rerank uses the same backbone architecture as Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B in a cross-encoder configuration. While the embedding model encodes queries and documents separately and scores their similarity, the reranker jointly encodes each query–document pair. A final multilayer perceptron (MLP) scoring head produces a scalar relevance logit.

All models are trained on a mixture of publicly available and synthetic multilingual, multimodal data, and their final released weights are produced through checkpoint ensembling. Further details on the training data are available in each model’s Hugging Face model card.

## 
		
	
	
		Nemotron 3.5 Parse

Enterprise knowledge often arrives in PDFs whose embedded text captures only part of what is on the page. Extracting that text can lose reading order, separate table values from their headers, or omit information conveyed in charts. Scanned documents and image-based PDFs may contain no usable text layer at all. Before this information can support search, retrieval, or automated document workflows, the pixels need to become structured content.

Nemotron 3.5 Parse converts document images into machine-readable text while preserving the structure that gives the content meaning. It identifies document elements, their locations, and reading order, and extracts tables and charts into structured representations. The resulting Markdown, HTML tables, and structured blocks give developers content that is better suited to indexing, search, and downstream processing. Applications can retrieve a passage with its surrounding context, process a table as rows and columns, and link extracted evidence back to its location on the original page.

At 631 million parameters, Nemotron 3.5 Parse brings this capability to document pipelines at scale, complementing Nemotron 3.5 Embed and Rerank with structured information for retrieval and agent workflows.

### 
		
	
	
		Leading Accuracy with Faster Document Processing

*Figure 8. Nemotron 3.5 Parse ranked first on ParseBench leaderboard among models with fewer than 1 billion parameters as of 10/20/2026.*

Nemotron 3.5 Parse ranks #1 on [ParseBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/llamaindex/ParseBench?leaderboard_max_params=1B) among models with fewer than 1 billion parameters, achieving a score of 75.20 while processing 10.5 pages per second on one NVIDIA H100. It delivers best-in-class speed with well optimized parameter allocation, multi-token prediction, speculative decoding and flexible native-resolution handling. ParseBench tests table and chart extraction, content faithfulness, semantic formatting, and visual grounding.

Developers can scale processing toward speed or accuracy using the same model. Single-pass inference extracts each page once for the highest throughput. Double-pass inference revisits tables and charts identified in the initial page parse. Triple-pass inference adds a detection pass to find additional regions for refinement. This approach concentrates additional processing on document regions that benefit from a closer look.

| Processing mode | ParseBench score ↑ | Pages per second on one H100 ↑ | 
|---|---|---|
| Single pass | 72.74 | 16.1 | 
| Double pass | 74.92 | 11.2 | 
| Triple pass | 75.20 | 10.5 | 

*Table 2. Model accuracy is able to scale with additional model passes at a small cost to throughput. Reprocessing focused crops of tables and charts leads to increased accuracy.*

All three configurations are Pareto optimal within this comparison: no other compared configuration achieves both higher accuracy and higher throughput. Teams can choose the operating point that fits their workload, from rapid ingestion of large document collections to more detailed extraction of complex pages.

*Figure 9.  Nemotron Parse 3.5 achieves pareto optimal performance on ParseBench leaderboard.*

### 
		
	
	
		How We Built Nemotron 3.5 Parse

Nemotron 3.5 Parse is trained on a diverse mixture of enterprise documents, scientific papers, forms, tables, charts, and multilingual text. A strong synthetic data engine expands the range of layouts, structures, and languages the model sees, complementing automatically labeled documents and human-labeled data. Synthetic multilingual data helps build broad OCR capability, with strong performance in evaluations spanning 163 language and script combinations. This diversity prepares the model for the varied content found in enterprise document collections. [Model card and multilingual coverage](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse).

We further improve robustness and reliability through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), using custom reward functions to reinforce correct document structure and penalize failures. This post-training reduces repetitive generation loops and unclosed blocks, improves table consistency, and strengthens adherence to chart schemas, making extracted information more reliable for downstream document workflows.

Thank you to LightOn for raising the open-source bar with their models and [technical blog](https://huggingface.co/blog/lightonai/lightonocr-3). The shared techniques were pivotal in improving our model.

## 
		
	
	
		Early Enterprise Partner Evaluations

- **Elastic** customers can access NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever embedding and reranking models through Elasticsearch’s Inference API using NVIDIA inference endpoints. Nemotron 3 will be available via Elastic Inference Service (EIS) soon, while support for Nemotron models on-prem deployment is on the roadmap.
- **Vectorize** evaluated NVIDIA [Nemotron 3.5 Embed using Hindsight Agent Memory](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/blog/2026/10/21/nemotron-3-5-embed-in-hindsight), and it ranked first on two long-conversation memory benchmarks: achieving 93.8% recall@10 on LoCoMo and 65.9% on BEAM 100K against seven other embedding models. It also delivered the highest MRR and recall@5, highlighting its strength for retrieving relevant memories across long, complex conversation histories.
- **Perplexity** saw strong results from NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Embed on Q2D-Web, its benchmark for first-stage retrieval in agentic search. On Perplexity's private 72-task reranking benchmark, NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B achieved the highest average score of the rerankers evaluated, with strong results across all six domains. These results show the value of specialized retrieval models alongside decision models like pplx-decider-v1.2. Perplexity looks forward to evaluating the Nemotron 3.5 retrieval suites, and the two companies are in ongoing discussions about deeper technical collaboration.
- **Turbopuffer** evaluated NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B on the enterprise PDF search benchmark and found that it provided \~5% more relevant results at Recall@20 than the next best model. These models are SOTA for common business tasks, like searching through PDFs with complex images, and are now available in Turbopuffer native embedding.

## 
		
	
	
		Getting Started

Developers can access the open weights, data, training recipes, and more on Hugging Face, deploy the [NVIDIA NIM](https://build.nvidia.com/explore/retrieval) for production inference, or deploy the models through leading AI Cloud and Inference Partners including Baseten ([Embed](https://www.baseten.co/library/nemotron-35-embed/), [Rerank](https://www.baseten.co/library/nemotron-35-rerank/), [Parse](https://www.baseten.co/library/nemotron-35-parse/)), [DeepInfra](https://deepinfra.com/blog/nvidia-nemotron-3.5-retrieval-release) ([Embed 1B](https://deepinfra.com/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16), [Embed 8B](https://deepinfra.com/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16), [Rerank 8B](https://deepinfra.com/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B-BF16)), [FriendliAI](https://friendli.ai/blog/nvidia-nemotron-retriever) ([Embed 1B](https://friendli.ai/models/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16), [Embed 8B](https://friendli.ai/models/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16), [Rerank 8B](https://friendli.ai/models/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B-BF16)), and OpenRouter ([Embed 1B,](https://openrouter.ai/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-embed-1b) [Embed 8B,](https://openrouter.ai/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-embed-8b) [Rerank 8B](https://openrouter.ai/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-rerank-8b)).

- **Nemotron-3.5-Parse:** [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse), [NIM](https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nim/nvidia/containers/nemotron-parse/-)
- **Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16:** [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16), [NIM](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/nemotron-3_5-embed-8b)
- **Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16:** [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16), [NIM](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/nemotron-3_5-embed-1b)
- **Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-NVFP4:** [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-NVFP4), [NIM](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/nemotron-3_5-embed-1b)
- **Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B-BF16:** [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B-BF16), [NIM](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/nemotron-3_5-rerank-8b)

For domain adaptation with NVIDIA AutoModel, we provide [fine-tuning](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Automodel/pull/3915) support for multimodal embedding and reranking, enabling teams to adapt the models to their own document collections and relevance requirements. Get started with the Nemotron [embedding](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Nemotron/tree/main/src/nemotron/recipes/embed) and [reranking](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Nemotron/tree/main/src/nemotron/recipes/rerank) fine-tuning recipes.

Choose a model based on your workflow: Parse for extracting structured information from documents, Embed for searching text and images, and Rerank for improving the ordering of retrieved results. Combine them to build retrieval pipelines that deliver stronger evidence to AI agents.

英伟达

特工的答案取决于它可以检索到的证据。当证据不完整或不相关时，代理将重复搜索并检查其他文档，在完成任务之前消耗更多的推理令牌。更好的检索可以帮助代理以更少的浪费令牌获得可靠的答案。在企业规模上，这种浪费会导致效率严重低下。代理需要正确的检索模型和系统才能更快地获得见解。

今天，我们正在扩展Nemotron Retriever系列，推出新的开放式商用模型，用于嵌入、重新排名和文档提取。新模型包括Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B BF16 、 1B BF16 、 1B NVFP4 、 Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B BF16和 631M 参数的Nemotron 3.5 Parse 。

这些最先进的模型共同为企业代理工作流程带来了多模式检索、相关性排名和文档处理。

更好的检索，更高效的代理

检索质量会影响代理生成的答案和 LLM 推理成本。相关证据可以帮助智能体回答问题或更好地决定下一步，而重新排序可以提高进入其上下文的证据的质量。

假设一位代理商被要求识别下季度有缺货风险的产品并解释原因。它必须结合图表中的需求预测、表格中的库存水平以及报告中的供应商交货时间，然后推断补货是否会在库存耗尽之前到达。完成任务需要跨文档找到相关证据并在分析中一起使用它们。

为了了解检索如何影响代理组合证据和完成任务的能力，我们评估了ViDoRe v3 、 BRIGHT和BrowseComp-Plus中的 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 和 Rerank 。 ViDoRe v3 使用组合的文本和图像输入，而 BRIGHT 和 BrowseComp-Plus 使用纯文本输入。在此管道中，代理使用搜索工具查询语料库，检查证据，并完善其下一次搜索尝试，以找到与给定查询最相关的信息。下面的实验改变了搜索工具的实现方式：仅嵌入、嵌入加重新排名，并且每种都使用不同的模型。当检索配置发生变化时，支持代理、工具、任务集、语料库和执行策略的 LLM 保持固定。我们衡量智能体查找每个任务相关信息的能力以及每个任务的智能体推理令牌总数，包括所有回合的输入和输出令牌。

图 1. 跨检索配置的端到端任务成功与每个任务的代理推理令牌总数。

  • 降低代理推理成本：添加 Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 可将 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B 的每次查询代理令牌成本降低约 14%，使用 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 1B 降低 13%，同时提高两种配置的检索准确性。
  • 相同代理预算内的更好证据：使用 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B 作为检索器，Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 在类似的代理令牌成本下比 Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B 提供了约 0.9 个点的 nDCG@10。

Nemotron 3.5 嵌入和重新排序

这些代理成功的背后是 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 和 Nemotron 3.5 Rerank，它们检索文本和图像中的证据，并根据代理的上下文对其进行优先级排序。 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 基于上一代 Nemotron 3 Embed 文本嵌入模型构建，可从文档图像中检索证据，包括表格、图表、信息图表、数据表和原理图。这允许应用程序搜索由视觉内容和文档文本传达的信息。

这四种模型提供了不同的检索和第二阶段排名选项：

模型角色部署重点
Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16 跨文本、图像检索证据，具有强大的多语言检索能力。对文本和视觉丰富的文档进行注重质量的搜索
Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16 将 8B 模型的多模态检索功能提炼为紧凑模型。具有较小模型占用空间的多模式索引和查询服务
Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-NVFP4 将 NVFP4 量化应用于文本和图像编码器，以实现高效的多模态推理。在支持的硬件上进行大规模文档索引和高吞吐量检索
Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B-BF16 联合评估查询-文档对，以优化文本和图像候选者的相关性排名。从检索到的候选者中选择 RAG 和代理工作流程的相关证据

表 1. Nemotron 3.5 Embed 和 Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 模型功能以及各种规模和变体的用例。

主要特点包括：

  • 文本和图像检索：搜索包含表格、图表、信息图表、数据表和原理图的文档文本和图像。
  • 多语言支持：在 34 种语言中评估文本检索，在 MIRACL Vision（18 种语言）和 KoViDoRe 上评估多语言视觉检索。该模型可能支持评估之外的其他语言。
  • 多模态重新排名：8B 交叉编码器对文本和图像输入上的查询-文档对进行评分。
  • BF16 和 NVFP4 部署：BF16 和 NVFP4 中提供 1B 嵌入模型，量化应用于文本和图像编码器。
  • 领域适应： Nemotron 嵌入微调配方支持自定义文档集合，在我们的图表和信息图实验中，Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16 和 Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16 的相对 nDCG@10 增益分别为 18% 和 3%。

ViDoRe v3 上领先的多模态密集检索

在ViDoRe v3.1上，Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B BF16 达到了 61.17 nDCG@10，在密集检索模型中排名第一。这比Llama Nemotron Embed VL 1B模型获得的 52.23 分提高了 8.94 分。 1B 模型将大部分视觉检索质量带入较小的模型中。 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 1B BF16 从 8B 教师中提炼出来，得分为 58.38 nDCG@10，保留了教师分数的 95.4%。

图 2. 截至 2026 年 10 月 20 日，Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B BF16 在 ViDoRe v3.1 排行榜上的密集检索模型中排名第一。

我们还将这些模型与 Qwen3-VL-Embedding、EmbeddingGemma-2 以及ViDoRe v3 、韩国 ViDoRe和MIRACL Vision的上一代 NVIDIA 模型进行了比较。下图报告了纯图像输入和图像与文本组合输入的检索准确性。

图 3. Nemotron 3.5 Embed 的文本和视觉检索性能与上一代模型和选定基线的比较。

多语言结果显示了模型如何跨不同语言设置检索证据。在MIRACL Vision上，8B 模型达到了 72.6 nDCG@10，比 Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B 高出 4.3 个点。我们还在KoViDoRe上评估了模型；当使用组合图像和文本输入时，Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B 和 1B 的性能均优于 Qwen 基线。

重新排列代理任务的证据

嵌入模型通过将内容表示为向量来使大型集合可搜索。检索返回候选集后，Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B BF16 根据查询评估每个候选，以优化文本和图像输入的排序。通过区分广泛相关的内容和直接回答问题的证据，重新排序器可以帮助代理更有效地使用他们的上下文预算，并专注于完成任务所需的信息。对于代理检索系统来说，尽早呈现最有力的证据可以减少分散注意力的上下文，并帮助代理产生更扎实、更有效的响应。

我们与 MTEB 团队合作，推出ViDoRe v3.1 重新排名排行榜，以对纯图像、纯文本以及组合图像和文本输入的文档检索重新排名者进行基准测试。 Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B BF16 通过组合图像和文本输入实现了 60.49 nDCG@10，而 Qwen-3-VL-Reranker-8B 为 59.17。

图 4. 截至 2026 年 10 月 20 日，Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B-BF16 在 ViDoRe v3.1 重新排名排行榜上排名第一。

图 5.Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B 与 Qwen 3 VL Reranker 8B 的文本和视觉重新排序性能比较。两个模型都对 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 1B 模型检索到的前 50 个候选对象进行了重新排名。

使用 NVFP4 扩展多模式检索

检索质量只是生产代理系统等式的一部分。随着文档集合和查询量的增长，团队必须平衡准确性、吞吐量和基础设施要求。

Nemotron 3.5 Embed 1B NVFP4 为高通量多模式检索提供了优化的部署选项。在 NVIDIA GB200 上，与 1B BF16 模型相比，它的吞吐量提高了 27.1%，从每秒 101.3 个文档增加到 128.8 个文档，同时在结合图像和文本输入的 ViDoRe v3 上保留了 99.85% 的检索精度。如图 6 所示，NVFP4 模型为跨生产工作负载扩展检索的团队提供了强大的准确性与吞吐量权衡。

这种部署灵活性补充了特定于领域的定制：团队可以选择适合其基础设施的模型权重的数据类型，然后根据自己的术语、文档和检索任务调整嵌入和重新排序模型。

图 6. ViDoRe V3 检索精度与服务效率的比较，将 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 与选定的较小开放嵌入基线进行比较。

使用 NVIDIA NIM 提供高性能服务

NVIDIA NIM 为 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 提供高性能部署路径。在 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 服务器版上进行测试时，NIM 每秒交付 6,031 个查询请求，大约是每秒 2,099 个请求的同类 vLLM 配置吞吐量的 2.9 倍，同时保持相当的通道处理吞吐量。这种优化的服务堆栈可帮助企业通过生产就绪的部署和支持来扩展检索工作负载。

使检索适应特定领域的任务

企业代理经常搜索包含通用检索模型可能无法完全捕获的专业术语和公司特定信息的文档。通过微调，团队可以使用自己的文档、查询和相关标签来调整 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 和 Rerank，以适应其特定领域和用例。

Nemotron 多模式嵌入微调方法将合成数据生成、硬负挖掘、使用NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel进行微调以及评估整合到一个工作流程中。团队可以从自己的文档生成查询和相关性标签，为检索任务构建训练数据。

我们使用 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 生成的 8,591 个合成查询对 8,202 个图表和信息图图像进行了评估，重点关注具有多个相关图像的枚举和开放式查询。对 Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16 对一个 epoch 的 6,872 个查询进行微调，将 nDCG@10 从 37.34 增加到 44.12，相对于基础模型（在 1,719 个保留的合成查询上）增加了 18%。使用相同的合成查询集，对一个时期的 Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16 进行微调，将 nDCG@10 从 41.44 增加到 42.75，相对增益增加了 3%。

我们如何构建嵌入和重新排序模型

Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B 基于Ministral-3-8B-Instruct构建，其语言组件从Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16初始化。该模型使用对比学习在图像和文本语料库上进行训练，以生成多模态检索的表示。

Embed 1B 模型是从 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B 中提炼出来的，其语言组件是从Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16初始化的。蒸馏结合了余弦和均方误差 (MSE) 损失，以使学生的嵌入与教师的嵌入保持一致。

在整个嵌入模型训练过程中，语言组件保持冻结状态。因此，纯文本嵌入预计将与相应的 Nemotron 3 Embed 模型保持不变，从而允许重复使用现有的文本嵌入和向量索引。

Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 在交叉编码器配置中使用与 Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B 相同的主干架构。嵌入模型分别对查询和文档进行编码并对其相似性进行评分，而重排序器则对每个查询-文档对进行联合编码。最终的多层感知器 (MLP) 评分头会生成标量相关性 logit。

所有模型都经过公开可用和合成的多语言、多模式数据的混合训练，其最终发布的权重是通过检查点集成产生的。有关训练数据的更多详细信息，请参阅每个模型的 Hugging Face 模型卡。

Nemotron 3.5 解析

企业知识通常以 PDF 形式提供，其嵌入文本仅捕获页面上的部分内容。提取该文本可能会丢失阅读顺序、将表值与其标题分开或忽略图表中传达的信息。扫描文档和基于图像的 PDF 可能根本不包含可用的文本层。在这些信息可以支持搜索、检索或自动化文档工作流程之前，像素需要变成结构化内容。

Nemotron 3.5 Parse 将文档图像转换为机器可读的文本，同时保留赋予内容含义的结构。它识别文档元素、它们的位置和阅读顺序，并将表格和图表提取为结构化表示。由此产生的 Markdown、HTML 表和结构化块为开发人员提供了更适合索引、搜索和下游处理的内容。应用程序可以检索段落及其周围的上下文，将表格处理为行和列，并将提取的证据链接回其在原始页面上的位置。

Nemotron 3.5 Parse 拥有 6.31 亿个参数，具有大规模记录管道的功能，通过用于检索和代理工作流程的结构化信息来补充 Nemotron 3.5 Embed 和 Rerank。
